description: Somos CuyOrbit, un equipo con experiencia en desarrollo de Software, IA/ML, sistemas georreferenciados y business dev. Parte del equipo gano el 1er puesto en Lima en NASA Space Apps 2025 y cuenta con trayectoria en hackatons. Desarrollamos SueloVision, una herramienta que combina datos de la nasa con informacion local del suelo y cultibos para ayudar a los agricultores a elegir rotaciones que protejan la salud del suelo.
summary:
Plotterra is a decision tool that helps farmers choose what to plant, in Huánuco, Peru and in farming regions around the world. The farmer maps their plot, and Plotterra compares three crop plans for the next three seasons: one that earns more money, one that saves water and one that cares for the soil. An AI assistant explains the results in plain language.

It addresses the challenge by turning NASA satellite and climate data into practical guidance for a changing climate. Each plan is tested against 100 simulated scenarios, including real past weather years, dry spells and price drops. Farmers see not only the best case but how often each plan holds up when conditions turn against them, so they can adapt before they invest.

This matters because planting decisions carry high risk and little margin for error, and a bad season can cost a family its income. Plotterra gives farmers the same kind of data-driven planning that large farms already use.
details:
We designed Plotterra around three steps: drawing the plot, comparing options and reviewing a plan. Farmers trace their land with a finger or a mouse and tell us their previous crop and how they get water. Our engine compares three-season rotations under 100 scenarios of weather, irrigation and prices.

We show estimated margins, water needs and risks. Farmers can also test changes, such as having less irrigation, and recalculate. We added an OpenAI-powered assistant to explain the results; the figures come from the engine.

We use NASA POWER for climate, HLS for crop greenness and ECOSTRESS for water-stress context in Ambo, along with CHIRPS and SoilGrids. We apply FAO-56 and FAO-33 to the water and yield calculations. We built the web app with React, TypeScript, Leaflet and Motion, and the backend with Python, FastAPI and SQLite.

Our proposal brings these calculations together in one visual comparison. We considered limited familiarity with digital tools: we use short instructions, read-aloud support and mobile-friendly controls. We want farmers to understand what changes between their options and to plan with greater clarity.
